q: A school-age child who reverses b and d and struggles to match or sort shapes most likely has a deficit in which visual perceptual skill?
w: Visual discrimination is noticing similarities and differences among forms. Its deficit shows as b/d reversals and trouble matching or sorting, one of the seven visual perceptual skills.
k: b/d reversal, poor matching = visual discrimination deficit.

q: A white pupil (leukocoria) found in a child must be urgently worked up to rule out:
w: Leukocoria is never normal and demands urgent evaluation to exclude retinoblastoma, the most common intraocular malignancy of childhood. Congenital cataract is another cause.
k: Leukocoria in a child = rule out retinoblastoma.

q: The approximate visual acuity of a newborn at birth is:
w: A newborn sees at roughly 20/800 with shadowy vision and no coordinated eye movements, then matures toward 20/20 over the first few years.
